transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, what brings me in is... I guess I just don't have the push I used to have anymore. I used to do choir, and my quilting, and going out visiting folks. But now, most days I just sit at home with the TV on low. I know people are expecting me to be places, but... I just sit there instead.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy, like choir or quilting?

Yes, doctor. Like I was just saying, that's exactly it. I just don't have the push for them anymore. I used to really care about my quilting and the singing, but... the interest is just gone now. I'd rather just sit there at home with the TV on low, even when I know folks are expecting me to show up.
How long have you been feeling this way, without the interest in your usual activities?
Well, it's been building up for a while now. I'd say it started since I retired from the school office... which was a little over two years ago.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the time, even when you're not thinking about changes in your life or retirement?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or depressed. I don't sit there crying or feeling bad about things... I just don't have the energy for it. It's not really a sad feeling, it's just... I just don't care to do much of anything anymore.
Do you feel that you have little to no energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much?

No, I wouldn't say I feel tired or out of energy like I need to sleep. It's not like that. I just... I just don't have the drive to get up and do things. My body feels fine, it's just the wanting to do things that's missing.
Do you find yourself feeling down or in a depressed mood most of the time, even when there's nothing specific bothering you?

Like I said just a minute ago, no, I don't feel depressed or sad. My mood is fine, really. I'm not walking around feeling down about things... I just don't have that want to do anything anymore. But no, I wouldn't call it feeling depressed.

Can you describe how you feel when you used to do things you enjoyed, like quilting or singing in the choir—did you stop getting any pleasure from them completely, or did you still enjoy them but just not feel like doing them?

I don't really know if I still enjoy them or not. I just... I haven't done them in so long. I used to like them, sure, but now I just don't have the urge to even try. It's not that I do them and don't like it, it's just that I don't do them at all anymore.
Do you find that you no longer take pleasure or interest in almost all activities, even ones you used to enjoy, most days?

Yeah, that's pretty much it. It's really what brings me in here... I just don't have the push I used to have for things. Not for choir, or quilting, or even visiting folks. Most days, I just sit at home. I'll have the TV on low, just sitting there... even though I know people are expecting me to show up. I just don't have the interest to go.
Do you feel like you're in a low mood or not yourself, even when things around you are fine and there's nothing specific bothering you?
Like I keep saying, no, it's not a low mood. I'm not sad or upset or anything like that. I just... I just don't have the energy or the want-to for anything. But I wouldn't say I'm feeling down.
Do you find it hard to focus or concentrate on things, like watching TV or reading, even when you're not distracted by other things?

No, I wouldn't say I have trouble focusing. Like I mentioned, I leave the TV on low and just sit there... I can follow along with what's happening on the screen just fine if I want to. I just don't really care to pay much attention to it. But my concentration itself is alright.
Would you say that you've completely lost interest in almost everything, even things you used to enjoy or found meaningful?

I think we just talked about that a minute ago... but yes, that's right. Like I said before, I just don't have the interest in much of anything anymore. The things I used to like doing, I just don't care to do them right now. That's really all there is to it.
Would you say that your lack of interest in doing things is total, meaning you don’t feel like doing anything at all anymore, even things you used to enjoy or found meaningful?

Well, I feel like we're going over the same ground here, doctor. I don't know about the word 'total,' but... like I was just saying a second ago, I just don't have the drive to do much of anything right now. The things I used to like, I just leave them be. I don't really know how else to explain it to you.
Can you describe your mood throughout the day—do you feel down or depressed most of the time, even when nothing in particular is wrong or bothering you?

No, I wouldn't say I feel down or depressed. I just feel... well, flat, I guess. I don't feel sad or anything like that. I'm just sitting here, not feeling much of anything. It's not like I'm crying or feeling miserable, I just don't have the energy or interest to do anything, like we were just talking about. But my mood itself isn't bad.
Can you remember the last time something truly made you feel happy or gave you a sense of pleasure, even just for a moment?

I... well, I'm not really sure. I can't rightly remember the last time I felt really happy about something. Nothing really stands out to me. Like I was saying, it's just been a whole lot of nothing lately... just that flat feeling. So, no, I can't really give you a specific time.
Would you say that you've completely stopped feeling pleasure or enjoyment in almost all activities, even ones you used to like?

Yes, I suppose that's right. I just don’t have the push I used to have for the things I liked... like my choir, or my quilting, or even visiting folks. I don't get any pleasure from them now. Most days I just sit at home with the TV on low. I know people are expecting me to show up to these things, but I just don't have it in me to go or enjoy it anymore.
How long has it been since you last felt interested or took pleasure in the things you used to enjoy?
Well, I suppose it's been a good while now. It feels like this has just been building up since I retired from the school office... which was a little over two years ago.
